appearance_facts.fact: Single blue line with circular markers connects 20 annual points from 1976 (left) to 1995 (right); a light purple fill spans from the line up to the top of the plot area.
The line reaches its lowest vertical position (largest downward extent) at the 1980 marker, which sits visibly below all other markers on the chart.
The 1976, 1977, and 1978 markers are near the top of the plot, above the 1980 marker.
The 1986 marker is a local high (relatively near the top) but remains above the 1980 marker in vertical position.
Markers from 1987 through 1995 oscillate in the upper-middle band, all positioned above the 1980 marker.

printed_facts.fact: Chart title: 'Year vs. Price in U.S. dollars per barrel'.
Y-axis label 'Count' with tick values 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 arranged top-to-bottom (0 at top, 35 near bottom).
Primary field 'Route escalation year' with options: 'Route 1980 escalation review', 'Route 1976 escalation review', 'Route 1986 mid-period review'.
Readonly fields: 'Program area' = 'Energy markets'; 'Review scope' = 'Historical petroleum price spike screening'; 'Record workflow' = 'Analyst escalation routing'.

public_definitions: Task: 'Review the historical petroleum price dashboard and route the year that should receive escalation follow-up for the highest per-barrel cost observed in this screening cycle.'
Chart reference: 'Historical petroleum price dashboard: Year and price in U.S. dollars per barrel'.
Applicable option condition: select the year corresponding to the highest per-barrel cost among the listed options (1980, 1976, 1986).
uncertain: The y-axis is labeled 'Count' and runs 0 (top) to 35 (bottom), which is inverted relative to a conventional price scale; the mapping of vertical position to 'highest per-barrel cost' is therefore ambiguous (the 1980 point is the lowest on the page but the largest tick value ~38, while 1976/1977/1978 are near the top with small tick values ~12–15).
No explicit dollar-per-barrel numeric annotations are printed on the markers, so exact price values cannot be read; only relative vertical positions and the inverted tick scale are available.
Whether 'highest per-barrel cost' should be interpreted as the maximum tick value (favoring 1980) or the highest visual position (favoring 1976/1977/1978) is unresolved.
